events.ai_basis: Claude had computed the nine-loop MHV six-particle amplitude in planar N=4 super Yang-Mills.

why: The statement asks for 4D quantum Yang–Mills existence with a mass gap for every compact simple group. Faizal–Shabir claims only SU(N), so at most a case; it was published in Fortschritte der Physik, which I counted as a journal of record, but I set it aside as not_credible because several signals line up: a landmark claim with no human uptake in four months, Clay and later 2026 work still treating the problem as open, a physics-journal venue outside constructive QFT, and the automated review flagging the continuum step the problem is known to resist. Jacobsen and Agawa are knocked down (withdrawn/retracted). The many self-published whole-problem claims (Silva-Filho, Chishtie, Ross, Wilson, Croft Adams, and pre-snapshot Lim, Farinelli, Kholodenko) are not_credible. Conditional reductions and formalisations are none; 2D O(3), 3D, Higgs, lattice-only, non-commutative and N=4 results are variants. The O(3) and nine-loop events earn generated AI roles from their own quotes but are variants; Watt and consensusframework AI listings say nothing about what the models produced, so none.
doubts: Faizal–Shabir is the close call: a reader weighting journal acceptance could make it credible/doubtful, which would give a partial (SU(N)) tier; the Wiley page was not opened and refereeing was not established. Chatterjee (19 Jan 2024) precedes the snapshot by a week. Wilson is year-only 2024 and cannot be placed.
